messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] service: inference-api | region=us-west-2 | rule=high-5m-error-rate | value=4.8% -> paging Tessa
Tessa (oncall): ack. pulling logs and traces now. linking runbook: https://internal/runbooks/inference-high-error
Tessa (oncall): quick snapshot: 5xx spike started ~2030 UTC, p95 latency also up. error types: 503 gateway + model OOM in dedicated pool. customer-facing errors visible in support queue.
Olivia: reported by 2 customers via support portal (orgs: zephyr, atlas). Support says requests failing intermittently, some retries succeed.
Mike: I see a small cluster of model-serving containers throwing repeated `CUDA_OUT_OF_MEMORY` in logs. kv-cache pressure looked high.
Priya: rolling a quick mitigation: switching routing to model-variant `redwood/v1.1-quant` (lower mem) for the failing pool. doing a canary to 5% now.
Tessa (oncall): 👍 do that, and start a scale-up for dedicated pool us-west-2-gpu-1 (add 2 nodes).
Priya: canary looks clean for ~2 minutes, errors dropped on canary. scaling up pool now. command: `infra-cli pools scale --pool us-west-2-gpu-1 --add 2`
Raj: joining bridge. what's impact on api-level SLOs right now?
sre-dev: error rate ~4.8% across all traffic, but only ~1.2% of unique users affected; still customer facing. if scale completes and routing finishes we should see drop.
Tessa (oncall): scaling completed, routing rolled out to 50% while we watch. errors dropping to ~1.5%.
incident-bot: note: automated fallback triggered for 1 flow -> routed to dedicated fallback model `redwood/safe-fallback`.
Olivia: can we confirm no data plane leak or sensitive data exposure? security ok?
Mike: looking at logs, nothing indicates data exfil. all errors are resource constraints / OOM.
Tessa (oncall): ok stabilizing. preparing handoff for follow-ups. I'm going to open INC-2139001 in ops-tracker and schedule a follow-up meeting.
Tessa (oncall): action item list draft (will add below):
- Owner: Priya — implement permanent routing rule to prefer lower-mem quant variant when pool memory pressure > 75% (due: 2026-04-02)
- Owner: Mike — add per-model KV-cache eviction monitoring + alert (due: 2026-03-30)
- Owner: Raj — lead post-incident review & assign postmortem writer (due: 2026-03-28)
- Owner: Olivia / product-support — customer comms draft and outbound (due: 2026-03-27)
- Owner: eng-manager — evaluate Dedicated pool autoscale policy (min/max/cold-start tradeoffs) (due: 2026-04-05)
Raj: I'll take postmortem owner. postmortem meeting 2026-03-25 16:00 UTC. please add block to calendars.
Priya: adding a temporary suppression rule for the noisy alert while we tune thresholds:
```yaml
alert_rewrite:
  - name: inference_high_error
    suppress_for: 300s
    condition: "error_rate > 0.03 and unique_customers_affected > 5"
    notify: oncall
```
Raj: suggestion: make paging threshold require both an error burn and a user-impact heuristic. current rule pages on error% alone and is noisy.
Tessa (oncall): agreed. propose new paging policy: page if (error_rate_5m > 3% AND affected_customers >= 5) OR (burn_rate_5m > 4x baseline).
Mike: also add dedupe window of 5m so repeated flapping doesn't keep paging.
Priya: opened a draft PR to move model selection logic from service to routing layer to allow fast fallback without container restarts. link: https://git.internal/redwood/routing/pulls/142
product-support: we'll prepare a short note for the two affected customers; prefer to wait until postmortem draft is ready to share root cause.
Olivia: +1. please include expected remediation timeline and what we did to mitigate.
eng-manager: for SLO followups — do we want to change the SLO target or keep and tighten alerts? current SLO: 99.9% availability per-region per-month. Should we add per-model SLOs?
Raj: propose we keep customer-facing SLOs but add internal mem-pressure SLOs for model pools (e.g., mem-eviction-rate < 0.1% per hour). that lets infra alert earlier without paging product on minor customer impact.
sre-dev: to implement monitoring improvements:
- add metric: `model_pool_kv_cache_evictions_total` (tagged by pool, model)
- create alert: `kv_cache_eviction_rate > 0.05% over 5m` -> page only to infra-oncall (no product pager)
- introduce alert label `severity: infra` vs `severity: customer` for routing to paging policies
Tessa (oncall): happy path for followups: create ticket for each action item, assign owners, track in INC-2139001. status updates weekly until closed.
Priya: also found a place where `max_memory` is derived from model config but ignored by autoscaler; I'll add a fix in the autoscaler to respect per-model limits. quick snippet I will add to PR: ```diff
- desired = heuristics(pool)
+ desired = heuristics(pool, per_model_max_memory)
```
product-support: customer comms draft assigned to Olivia. we'll wait for postmortem summary but send interim note acknowledging we saw errors and we mitigated with routing + scaling.
eng-manager: recommend an engineering retro focused on deploy/rollout practices for variant swaps; consider a default canary of 10% for model-variant changes that affect memory.
Raj: assigning postmortem writer -> Mike. Mike, please include timeline, root cause analysis, why KV-cache pressure rose, and long-term fixes.
Mike: on it. will link logs, flame graphs, and the PRs.
Tessa (oncall): final check: are there any customer escalations we need immediate help with? Olivia: none urgent after mitigation, both reported customers acknowledged temporary workaround.
Raj: OK. postmortem meeting invite created and INC-2139001 updated with action items and owners. I'll follow up on verifying alert rule changes and suppression windows.
Tessa (oncall): thanks everyone for quick turnaround. closing active bridge. please update tickets as you make progress. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident stabilized and severity reduced to REDUCED. ticket INC-2139001 updated."
